summary: Tested Settings API + UI and Mikrotik auto-comment/rate-limit on quick-register. 7/7 backend pytest cases pass; full Playwright frontend flow (sidebar routing, section rendering, save, persistence-after-reload, restore) passes. Cleaned up all TEST_ routers/plans/leases/customers.
critical_code_review_comments: SettingsController::update returns HTTP 200 but the JSON envelope key is 'status' (='success'), not 'success'; the rest of the API standardizes on {'success': true, ...}. Consider aligning for consistency (non-blocking; UI works because it inspects res.data.keys directly).

MikrotikService::updateOrMakeStaticLease correctly early-exits when connection_status in ['offline','unknown',null] with skipped=true — verified: no TCP attempt, request returns in ms. Also correctly re-looks up '.id' after make-static (RouterOS resets the id on that op).
UnregisteredLeaseController::quickRegister writes local dhcp_leases.comment/rate_limit/is_dynamic after DB commit, so UI stays consistent even when router is unreachable — verified in DB.
Setting model uses Cache::rememberForever; write path calls Cache::forget both in put() and again in controller — belt-and-braces, no cache-staleness bug observed under PUT then GET.
seed_data_creation: Per-test TEST_ prefixed router+plan+lease created via direct SQL, cleaned up in fixture teardown; also company.name & billing.vat_percent PUT-then-restored to defaults 'Solarnet Internet' / 12.0.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Login response shape is {status:'success', data:{access_token, token_type, expires_in, user}} — NOT 'token'. dhcp_leases table requires non-null 'server' column ('default' is fine). All Settings PUT writes must go through /api/v1/settings so the Setting model can bust its cache; do not INSERT into settings directly. MikroTik in this preview is always offline (guard path validated) — do not attempt to bring up a real router.
